qualifyingSuccessorRule: a C24 primary of a Track I procedure (population L, B or F × selector original or RA1) is a qualifying successor iff (a) it passed Q1–Q6 at C24; (b) its procedure’s sequential chronological verdict is supported; (c) it is not dominated by New L0 (C24 evidence, same instrument) on (centre net, centre DD) nor on (confirmation p10, confirmation p90 DD); (d) it has materially stronger downside risk than New L0 on the C24 evidence: confirmation worst-10% mean DD ≤ New L0’s − $2,500, centre DD ≤ New L0’s + $2,500, worst per-lot MAE ≥ New L0’s − $2,500; (e) it passes V1–V3 once on FULL. Track N and U primaries are incumbent-informed with no independent chronological test and are never qualifying successors; RA2 is a secondary ablation. Otherwise: research-only (with the reason). "No qualifying successor" is a valid outcome. Deployment would still need the user’s decision.
